Explore how reinforcement learning, language models and AI safety developed through papers, people and institutions. The focus is on alignment, agent reliability and catastrophic-risk research, with most institutional coverage from the US and UK.

Browse the [timeline](#the-map), follow a [reading route](#questions-through-the-history), or explore [people and institutions](#institutions-and-people). The [glossary](#glossary) explains terms used in the cards.

## The map

Choose an era or event to read its explanation and follow related work. Earlier decades take less horizontal space than recent years; the overview shows all years on a linear scale.

::: {.column-screen-inset}
```{=html}
<div data-atlas="map"></div>
```
:::

## Questions through the history

Each route follows a research question across papers. Start with “How does an agent learn from reward?” for RL foundations, or “Where did RLHF come from, and what did each step add?” for the path to assistants. Other routes cover reward failures, oversight, interpretability and deception.

::: {.column-page}

```{=html}
<div data-atlas="routes"></div>
```

## Sources and method

Dates refer to the publication, announcement or event named in each card. Some cards also discuss later work; their date notes explain which milestone anchors them on the timeline. The links between cards describe research dependencies or comparisons. “Parallel” marks a comparison without claiming direct influence.

I compiled the atlas with AI assistance and checked selected claims against primary sources. Some details rely on secondary reporting, and unresolved dates are flagged in the cards. Each study's task, models and limitations matter when interpreting its results.

Compute estimates come from a saved [Epoch AI dataset](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-models), under CC BY 4.0. The step line follows the largest documented training-compute estimate up to each date; the labelled dots are selected examples. The scale is logarithmic. Estimates have uncertainty, and unpublished training details leave gaps in the record. The chart's method panel includes the data, snapshot and calculation details.
